inlines.text: A patient must have 1.2 L of fluid over 4 hours through an intravenous drip.
How many drops per minute are required?
What is the drop rate per minute if 1.3 L of fluid is to be delivered over 6 h with 12 drops/mL?
The three quantities are volume, time and drops.

inlines.latex: \begin{aligned}\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}&=\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Volume}}\times\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Time}}\\\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}&=\frac{12\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\times\frac{1.3\text{ L}}{6\text{ h}}\\\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}&=\frac{12\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\times\frac{1300\text{ mL}}{360\text{ min}}\\\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}&=\frac{130}{3}\text{ drops/min}\\\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Time}}&=43.3\dot{3}\text{ drops/min}\end{aligned}

inlines.text: Calculate how long it will take to deliver 800 mL at 20 drops/min if there are 25 drops/mL.

answer.worked:
Quantities: volume, time and drops.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{Time}}{\text{Volume}}&=\frac{\text{Time}}{\text{Drops}}\times\frac{\text{Drops}}{\text{Volume}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{800\text{ mL}}&=\frac{1\text{ min}}{20\text{ drops}}\times\frac{25\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{800\text{ mL}}&=\frac{25\text{ min}}{20\text{ mL}}\\x&=800\times\frac{25}{20}\\x&=1000\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Distance}}&=\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Volume}}\times\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Distance}}\\\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Distance}}&=\frac{\$1.85}{1\text{ L}}\times\frac{8.2\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}\\\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Distance}}&=\$0.1517/\text{km}\\\frac{\text{Cost}}{\text{Distance}}&\approx\$0.152/\text{km}\end{align*}$$
Rounded to 3 decimal places.
